newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nervous German coffee roasters eye tight supply.
newsitem.headline: Nervous German coffee roasters eye tight supply.

text.p: Outright coffee prices in Germany rose on nearby tightness as origin exports were delayed and roasters bought hand-to-mouth, traders said on Monday.

"Spot coffees are hard to get...Central Americans are being shipped and Colombia seems to have solved its truckers' strike problem, but the arrivals are being pushed back to the end of November," one said.
"This is causing concern -- some roasters have gaps in their cover for certain blends and traders have made speculative purchases to squeeze out high premiums."
African arabicas were also tight and expensive, and the fighting in Zaire added to the firmer tone.
But the traders did not see the tightness lasting far beyond the end of the year.
Brazils were readily available and consumption in that area of the market was stagnant, they added.
The German coffee industry association DKV said last week roasted coffee sales were likely to be steady this year after a 2.5 percent fall in 1995.
Traders said coffee inventories across the Atlantic were even tighter than in Europe and this could boost the New York arabica December position.
U.S. certified stocks were down to just 5,538 bags last week and figures to be released after the close of business were not expected to show higher levels.
December last Friday ended down 1.45 cents/lb at 116, but had a 11.9 cents premium over March.
In the Bremen import market, arabicas rose $6-12 per 50 kg fob on the week with Brazils up $6 at $112 and with Colombia Excelso at $140, up $12.
